channel.title: The Wilson Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Wilson Times (wilsontimes.com)

item.title: For Your Health: Colonoscopy is a simple test that saves lives
item.description: Colonoscopy, a safe screening starting at age 45, can remove precancerous polyps and lower the risk of death from colorectal cancer, the second leading cause of U.S. cancer-related deaths.

item.title: Behind closed doors
item.description: Shoppers at JCPenney walked through these doors for many years. Now the building is coming down with the demolition of Wilson Mall.

item.title: Thrift shop helps out local organizations
item.description: West Nash United Methodist Church Thrift Shop donated $128,000 to 18 nonprofits in 2025, supporting Wilson County residents through the volunteer-run shop.

item.title: Deputies: Car theft suspect hid in warehouse
item.description: Deputies say a juvenile who repeatedly stole the same car was tracked by GPS, fled a traffic stop and hid in a Wilson warehouse before a police K-9 found him; he now faces multiple felony charges.

item.title: Area Calendar, March 13-14, 2026
item.description: Area sports schedule for March 13-14, 2026, features Barton College teams on the road and at home, high school baseball, softball, soccer and lacrosse, plus Fike in the 5-A basketball championship.

item.title: AREA ROUNDUP: Garris gets RBI, win for Knights
item.description: Area roundup: Garris sparks Greenfield’s first win; Southern Nash baseball takes Big East lead, softball improves to 6-0; Fike boys golf claims second 5-A/6-A Big East match.

item.title: Tigers don’t panic, just defend their way to title
item.description: Wilson Prep girls overcome a 1-for-18 night from three, leaning on defense and My’Angel Brimage’s dominance to beat Robbinsville 58-44 for the NCHSAA 1-A title and a 26th straight win.

item.title: The Brittany XX by the Numbers
item.description: The Brittany XX will bring a record 91 high school girls soccer teams for 64 games over two days in Wilson, featuring state champions, top‑25 programs and schools from 33 N.C. counties.

item.title: The Brittany XX the biggest yet with 91 teams playing 64 games
item.description: Marking its 21st year, The Brittany XX girls soccer showcase brings a record 91 teams for 64 games at Gillette Soccer Complex, honoring the memory of Brittany Willis with matchups of teams from across North Carolina
